title: perf-bench-latency-throughput-personal-notes
content:
Personal perf experiment scratchpad - latency & throughput runs

Context:
- Quick micro-benchmarks to validate batching/quantization impact on our 8K-context transformer variants. Running locally on dev rig (single node, 1x A100-80GB, CUDA 12.1, pytorch 2.2 + custom kernels). Goal: surface regressions and identify good default batch/seq combos for Dedicated.

Hardware / env:
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (driver 535.xx)
- CPU: 32 vCPU Intel (cloud dev instance)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Runtime: custom-redwood-infer-v0.9.3 (serving runtime w/continuous batching)
- Model: rw-8k-gptq-4bit (quantized) / rw-8k-fp16 baseline
- Workload runner: tools/bench/throughput_runner.py (local)
- Notes: pinned to CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, turned off other background processes

Commands used:
- baseline fp16 single-request latency:
  python tools/bench/latency.py --model rw-8k-fp16 --seq 256 --repeats 200 --batch 1
- quantized throughput sweep:
  python tools/bench/throughput.py --model rw-8k-gptq-4bit --seq 1024 --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8,16 --duration 120

Key raw results (median of runs / quick notes):
1) Latency (single-request, cold vs warm cache) - seq=256, tokens_out=64
- fp16 baseline: cold p50=42ms, cold p95=120ms; warm p50=28ms, warm p95=65ms
- gptq-4bit: cold p50=55ms, cold p95=160ms; warm p50=36ms, warm p95=95ms
  - Observations: quantization adds ~25-40% latency on single request; warm effects significant due to KV cache priming and kernel compilation overhead on first runs.

2) Throughput (tokens/sec) - seq=1024, output 128 tokens, duration 120s
- fp16 throughput by batch size (tokens/sec):
  b1: 1.2k tps
  b2: 2.1k tps
  b4: 3.6k tps
  b8: 4.9k tps
  b16: 5.1k tps (diminishing returns)
- gptq-4bit throughput by batch size (tokens/sec):
  b1: 1.0k tps
  b2: 1.9k tps
  b4: 3.4k tps
  b8: 4.6k tps
  b16: 4.8k tps
  - Notes: quantized model lower absolute throughput but similar scaling with batch size. Bottleneck shifts: FP16 limited by memory bandwidth, GPTQ limited by kernel efficiency for small matrices.

3) Latency vs batching tradeoff (seq=512)
- Target SLO: p95 < 200ms for interactive flows
- Observed: for gptq-4bit, batch sizes >4 push p95 > 200ms for seq 512; for fp16 batch up to 8 keeps p95 ~180ms.

Quick ASCII chart (throughput vs batch, seq=1024):
- fp16:  | b1=1.2k | b2=2.1k | b4=3.6k || b8=4.9k || b16=5.1k |
- gptq:  | b1=1.0k | b2=1.9k | b4=3.4k || b8=4.6k || b16=4.8k |

Short conclusions / heuristics:
- For low-latency interactive endpoints (seq <= 512, p95 <= 200ms), prefer fp16 with batch cap 4-8 depending on target SLO.
- For cost-sensitive high-throughput inference (background tasks, long-form generation), gptq-4bit with larger batch sizes gives better unit-cost even though absolute throughput slightly lower; quantization helps GPU memory utilization (more concurrent replicas).
- Warm-up matters: first-minute latencies can be 2x due to kernel priming; include warmup traffic or precompile kernels for production traffic.
- Auto-batching policies should cap batch sizes based on seq-length distribution (adaptive cap: max_batch = min(16, floor(8192 / avg_seq_len))).

Open questions / next runs:
- Re-run with multi-threaded IO disabled to ensure no CPU scheduling artifacts (ticket ENG-1012)
- Test same configs on A10 vs A100 (cost/throughput delta)
- Try newer kernel build (v0.9.4) that claims ~15% perf on GPTQ paths
- Add p99 measurements for tail latency analysis

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run quantized throughput with v0.9.4 (assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Add p99 measurement and store full traces (assigned: me)
- [ ] Add the best config to dedicated-config suggestions doc (link to PR once validated)

Notes-to-self:
- Save full run logs to /mnt/bench-results/2025-01-15/ (compress and upload to S3)
- When drafting docs, call out warm-up cost explicitly and recommend an "initial-warmup" flag for Dedicated deployments

Related links: PR #412 (kernel fixes), ENG-987
